name: Silverbird
rangeDescription: Southwestern and southern sudan, south sudan, western ethiopia, eastern uganda, western kenya, and northern tanzania
description: A beautiful, distinctive, and simply marked flycatcher with silvery gray upperparts and orange underparts. Juveniles are buff-and-gray, lacking orange, and are covered in complex scalloped markings.

name: Dusky Nightjar
rangeDescription: Montane forest of costa rica and western panama
description: Small dark nightjar with very limited range in the highlands of Costa Rica and Panama. Few obvious plumage features: entire body is intricately patterned with dark brown, black, and buff.

name: Tiny Sunbird
rangeDescription: Sierra leone to cameroon, gabon, eastern democratic republic of the congo, and western uganda; bioko
description: The smallest member of a group of frustratingly similar double-collared sunbirds that co-occur in African forests. Often encountered near forest edges and in forest clearings, and sometimes even in villages and gardens.

name: Beaudouin's Snake-Eagle
rangeDescription: Southwestern mauritania southward to guinea, eastward to southwestern sudan and western south sudan, possibly to northern uganda
description: Chunky dark brown raptor with a white belly marked by thin bars. Immatures are brown when perched, and show rufous patches in the underwing in flight.

name: Spot-tailed Nightjar
rangeDescription: Locally from southeastern mexico to northern bolivia, eastern paraguay, and southeastern brazil
description: Small nightjar of savanna and grassland with scattered bushes and palmettos. Spends the day roosting cryptically on the ground, but at night may be found beside quiet roads and tracks.

name: Mottle-backed Elaenia
rangeDescription: Tropical southeastern colombia to eastern ecuador, eastern peru, and western bolivia
description: Large elaenia with a striking headdress. It inhabits lightly-wooded areas, such as overgrown clearings, forest edge, and river islands, along the eastern base of the Andes.

name: Scripps's Murrelet
rangeDescription: Channel islands and islands off western coast of baja california
description: Small seabird, black above and white below. Breeds on rocky islands; otherwise found in warm offshore waters.

name: Snares Penguin
rangeDescription: Snares islands and adjacent waters off new zealand
description: Medium-sized crested penguin, endemic to New Zealand. Note the thin, vivid yellow eyebrow that droops behind the eye to form a bushy tufted crest.

name: Brown-breasted Kingfisher
rangeDescription: Philippines
description: A fairly large kingfisher of lowland and foothill open country and forest edge. Chocolate brown on the underparts and hood, down to the upper back.

name: Bougainville Fantail
rangeDescription: Montane forest of bougainville (northwestern solomon islands)
description: Small and drab with a long, often fanned tail. Mostly gray-brown above and slightly lighter tawny below, with a grayish head and a white eyebrow.

name: Guianan Tyrannulet
rangeDescription: Eastern venezuela, the guianas, and northeastern brazil north of the amazon river and east of the rio branco and rio negro; populations south of the amazon river (west to the lower rio madeira, eastward to ceará and alagoas) included here, but may represent an undescribed taxon
description: Tiny, inconspicuous flycatcher; in addition to small size, note stubby bill, wing bars, and longish tail. Found in a variety of forest habitats including primary and secondary rainforest, low-stature forests with sandy soils, and along river edges.

name: Rufous-tailed Xenops
rangeDescription: Southeastern colombia to southern venezuela, the guianas, eastern peru, and amazonian brazil
description: Small xenops of mature rainforest. Extensively streaked, tan body, with contrasting reddish wings and tail.

name: Vulturine Parrot
rangeDescription: Humid forest of eastern amazonian brazil south of the amazon
description: Medium-sized, largely green parrot with a striking head pattern. The head is featherless with a combination of orange, black, and yellow bristles.

name: Gough Island Finch
rangeDescription: Gough (southern atlantic ocean)
description: A large striking finch with a dagger-like bill and different looking sexes. Male is mostly olive with a black throat and yellow eye-ring and moustache; female is brownish and lacks the black throat.

name: Puff-backed Bulbul
rangeDescription: The thai-malay peninsula, sumatra, bangka island, and borneo
description: Brown bulbul with a sparse, wispy crest. Darker above and paler below.

name: Maroon-fronted Parrot
rangeDescription: Mountains of eastern mexico (sierra madre oriental)
description: Very local, long-tailed, and social parrot of mountains endemic to northeast Mexico. Feeds in pine and pine-oak forests and adjacent semiopen areas with orchards and flowering century plants.

name: Samoan Flycatcher
rangeDescription: Samoa (savai'i and upolu)
description: A small flycatcher. Male is deep glossy blue-black on the back, head, and tail.

name: Orange Bullfinch
rangeDescription: Montane forest of northern pakistan to northwestern india (himachal pradesh)
description: A small, brightly colored bullfinch. The male is orange with black mask, wings, and tail.

name: Gray-cheeked Parakeet
rangeDescription: Arid scrub of western ecuador and far northwestern peru
description: Small parakeet, fairly common within very limited range in southwest Ecuador and barely into extreme northwest Peru. Overall lime-green with pale gray head and sky-blue crown.

name: Yellow-shouldered Amazon
rangeDescription: Coastal northern venezuela including islas margarita and la blanquilla; bonaire
description: Large green parrot of desert Caribbean areas, including mainland. All green with yellow face, yellow shoulder patch, and orange wing patch.
